note: Power constants of energy_apps.py. All are vendor ceilings (TDP), not measurements of our builds: they bound the power from above and should be replaced by measured board power once available.

v80_card_w.meaning: AMD Alveo V80 card power, charged in proportion to the usable LUTs a design occupies
v80_card_w.source: AMD DS1013 (Alveo V80 data sheet), Product Details: thermal design power 190 W, passive cooling

cpu_package_w.meaning: package power of the CPU the decode timings ran on (graham, AMD EPYC 7713P)
cpu_package_w.checked: 2026-11-12, amd.com product page: 64 cores, default TDP 225 W (configurable 225-240 W)

cpu_cores.meaning: cores of that CPU; power per core = cpu_package_w / cpu_cores (package only: no memory, no cooling)

qubits_per_readout_line.meaning: qubits one synthesized discriminator instance reads (tab:fpga_resources is for five-qubit readout)

qpu_w_per_qubit.meaning: wall power per physical qubit of the QPU: dilution refrigerator, chilled water and room-temperature control electronics. Flat per qubit in both scenarios.
qpu_w_per_qubit.source: scaled: Parker and Vermeer, RAND working paper WR-A2427-3 (arXiv:2304.14344), 2023: a refrigerator drawing about 26 kW and holding 4,158 qubits (IBM Quantum System Two) gives 6.25 W/qubit; the authors call it extremely rough. today: Arute et al., Nature 574, 505 (2019), supplement (arXiv:1910.11333): 26 kW in total for the 53-qubit Sycamore (refrigerator ~10 kW, chilled water 10 kW or more, supporting electronics nearly 3 kW), i.e. 26000/53 W/qubit.
qpu_w_per_qubit.checked: 2026-11-12, both read from the papers' text

discriminator_w_per_lut.meaning: power per occupied LUT of the discriminator FPGA (ZCU216, xczu49dr). null = assume the V80's power per usable LUT
discriminator_w_per_lut.source: assumption: no power report exists for the hls4ml builds
